rules: Searched every PubMed record in Europe PMC with iodine (iodine, iodide, iodised salt, iodized salt, iodate) in its title or abstract, in papers about supplements, iodised salt, intake, diet or deficiency; downloaded all reviews, randomised trials and guidelines.
Left out animal studies (MeSH tags, or the title when there are none) and retracted papers.
An outcome counts when its words are in the title.

Reviews: meta-analyses or systematic reviews of randomised trials of giving iodine, with iodine in the title, or in the abstract of a review of several supplements (not reviews of blood levels in observational studies; reviews without an abstract are kept for screening), and not about another group of people (such as sepsis, intensive care or surgery; each outcome's list is in the search definition). Chosen: the three newest meta-analyses (systematic reviews only if fewer than three), plus the most comprehensive one (most trials pooled, read from the abstract). Citations are shown but do not choose.
Newer large trials: randomised trials of at least 1,000 people (read from the abstract) from the year of the newest chosen review on, which those reviews may not include.

Historical screening decisions and review choices are retained. Exact screening inputs and per-decision model provenance were not recorded, so they are not validated for current inputs. Legacy file attribution is shown per outcome; these decisions need fresh screening before a new build may select them.
Overlap is not shown: a bibliography can cite background or excluded trials and cannot establish which studies a review included or pooled.

left.title: Iodine supplementation for preventing iodine deficiency disorders in children and adolescents
left.reason: Iodine vs placebo with cognitive outcomes, but supplements were given directly to children and adolescents, not pregnant women.

left.reason: Covers maternal iodine in mild-to-moderate deficiency and child neurodevelopment, but is a narrative update that does not pool trials itself.

left.title: Iodine status during child development and hearing ability: a systematic review
left.reason: Includes an RCT in mildly iodine-deficient pregnant women, but the outcome is child hearing, not thinking, language, motor skills or IQ.

left.reason: Assesses breast milk iodine as a biomarker of iodine status, not supplementation effects on child development.

left.title: Insufficient iodine intake in pregnant women in different regions of the world: a systematic review
left.reason: Looks at how much iodine pregnant women get, not at the effect of supplements on child development.

left.reason: Iodine vs placebo with Bayley neurodevelopment outcomes, but supplements were given to preterm infants, not pregnant women.

left.reason: Meta-analysis of observational cohorts on maternal iodine status and child IQ, with no supplementation trials.

left.reason: Iodine vs placebo or no intervention in pregnant women and children, but outcomes are prenatal and postnatal growth, not neurodevelopment.

left.reason: Withdrawn review of iodine supplements given directly to children, not pregnant women; cognitive outcomes were summarised narratively, not pooled.

left.title: Nutrition (Micronutrients) in Child Growth and Development: A Systematic Review on Current Evidence, Recommendations and Opportunities for Further Research

left.title: Systematic review of the effects of iodised salt and iodine supplements on prenatal and postnatal growth: study protocol
left.reason: A protocol with no results, and its outcome is physical growth rather than cognitive or motor development.

left.reason: Iodine supplements for preterm infants, not pregnant women; the single included trial did not assess neurodevelopment.

question.population: Children aged 5 and under in iodine-deficient areas (through their mothers in pregnancy, or as infants)
question.intervention: Iodine supplements, iodised salt or iodised oil

screening.by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

left.title: Iodine supplementation for preventing iodine deficiency disorders in children and adolescents
left.reason: Pooled RCTs of iodine vs placebo with cognitive outcomes, but the population is mostly children aged 6 to 17; only one trial was in infants.

left.title: Iodine status during child development and hearing ability: a systematic review
left.reason: The outcome is hearing, not mental development, and most included studies are observational.

left.title: Breast Milk Iodine Concentration (BMIC) as a Biomarker of Iodine Status in Lactating Women and Children <2 Years of Age: A Systematic Review
left.reason: This review tests breast milk iodine as a status biomarker and does not look at iodine interventions or mental development.

left.title: Iodine supplementation for the prevention of mortality and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants
left.reason: Pooled RCTs of iodine vs placebo with Bayley cognitive scores, but the population is preterm infants rather than children in iodine-deficient areas.

left.title: Association of Maternal Iodine Status With Child IQ: A Meta-Analysis of Individual Participant Data
left.reason: An observational cohort meta-analysis of maternal iodine status and child IQ, with no iodine intervention.

left.title: WITHDRAWN: Iodine supplementation for preventing iodine deficiency disorders in children
left.reason: Iodine for children in iodine-deficient areas with cognitive outcomes, but it is withdrawn, mixes non-randomised trials, covers all ages and did no pooling.

left.title: Feeding the brain - The effects of micronutrient interventions on cognitive performance among school-aged children: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials
left.reason: RCTs of micronutrients including iodine on cognition, but the population is school-aged children aged 4 to 18, and it did no pooling.

left.title: Nutrition (Micronutrients) in Child Growth and Development: A Systematic Review on Current Evidence, Recommendations and Opportunities for Further Research
left.reason: A broad overview of many micronutrients, including iodine, in pregnancy and childhood, with no specific pooled iodine analysis.

left.title: A meta-analysis combining parallel and cross-over randomized controlled trials to assess impact of iodine fortified foods on urinary iodine concentration among children
left.reason: Pooled RCTs of iodine-fortified foods in children, but the outcome is only urinary iodine, not mental development.

left.title: Iodine supplementation for the prevention of mortality and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants
left.reason: An iodine RCT in preterm infants, a different group, and the included trial did not measure neurodevelopment.

left.title: The effects of iodine on intelligence in children: a meta-analysis of studies conducted in China
left.reason: Iodine in pregnancy vs ongoing deficiency with child IQ matches, but it pooled non-randomised Chinese comparison studies of children under 16, not RCTs.

left.title: Iodine supplementation for preventing iodine deficiency disorders in children
left.reason: Iodine for children in iodine-deficient areas with cognitive outcomes, but it mixes non-randomised trials, covers all ages and did no pooling.

left.title: [Meta-analysis on the relationship between children's intelligence and factors as iodine deficiency, supplement iodine and excessive iodine]
left.reason: Iodine correction vs none with IQ in deficient areas matches, but it pooled non-randomised studies of children aged 5-15, not RCTs.
